newsitem.title: USA: Ferro to take $100 mln post tax charge in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Ferro to take $100 mln post tax charge in Q2.

text.p: Ferro Corp said it will take a charge to income of approximately $100 million after tax in the second quarter for costs associated with the reduction of the company's worldwide manufacturing operations from approximately 80 to 50 facilities.

"Full implementation of the plan is intended to enable Ferro to achieve its goal of gross margins of 28 percent by the end of 1999, an increase of three percentage points over the 25 percent achieved during 1996," the specialty chemicals maker said in a statement.
The charge before tax is $153.0 million.

The pretax amount includes the write-off and write-down of assets, severance charges and other costs related to the realignment plan and Ferro said the net cash cost of the plan is approximately $38 million over a three-year period.
It estimates that, when completed, the plan should improve operating profit by more than $30 million a year.

The company said that attrition and consolidation and the sale of facilities should cut employment by 1,200 people over a three-year period from 6,900 now and cutbacks would take place mainly outside of the United States.
Annual capital expenditures associated with the facilities to be closed are approximately $15 million.
"Most of the specifics called for in our plan will take place in the first two years of the three-year plan," said Hector Ortino, Ferro's president and chief operating officer.
